subject: Monetary.ai reserved capacity regression - 5xx spikes & latency
messages:
From: John Park <ops@monetary.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Monetary.ai reserved capacity regression - 5xx spikes & latency

Vivek/Marissa —

We started seeing a regression across our inference traffic to the dedicated pool you manage starting ~08:45 PT. Impact summary:
- 95th p90 latency jumped from ~320ms to ~2.1s for our normal profile (seq len 512)
- 5xx rate increased to 3.2% from 0.1% (sustained for ~25m)
- Throughput dropped ~28% against our reserved commit (token/sec) leading to queueing at our side

We attached logs (monetary_logs_20260818.txt) and included a snapshot from our dashboard. This is affecting production and user-facing features for several of our merchants. We need immediate mitigation and an ETA for a fix. Please confirm receipt and next steps — if this needs escalation to your execs, let us know who to loop.

John Park
Head of Platform, Monetary.ai
ops@monetary.ai

Attachments: monetary_logs_20260818.txt
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: John Park <ops@monetary.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Monetary.ai reserved capacity regression - 5xx spikes & latency

John —

Thanks for the note and the logs, confirmed received. We're treating this as high priority. Quick acknowledgment and immediate actions:
1) I'm standing up an incident bridge with infra now (link in the runbook I just shared internally).
2) Can you confirm whether you saw a region shift (any APAC->US routing) or a sudden spike in avg sequence length? That helps rule out model-side regressions.
3) We're going to temporarily increase headroom on your dedicated pool (if available) while we triage to prevent further queueing — I'll confirm within 15 minutes.

I'll keep you posted on the bridge rollup and expected mitigation. Apologies for the disruption — we'll aim for a rollback/fix within the hour depending on root cause.

— Vivek
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Monetary.ai reserved capacity regression - 5xx spikes & latency

Vivek / team —

Summary of what ops sees so far and immediate mitigation plan (triage notes):
- Initial signal matches a kernel-selection regression introduced in the latest runtime rollout for the aarch64 kernels (we are seeing a subset of host pins choose a fallback execution path that is ~6-7x slower for medium-length sequences).
- Autoscaler attempted to rebalance but did not provision extra reserved nodes because a health-check flapped early in the scale-up probe. That left headroom artificially low for ~20m.

Short-term (next 0–60m):
- Roll back the kernel-selection change on the affected fleet subset (hotfix rolling to 25% of nodes immediately).
- Manually add two reserved nodes to Monetary.ai's pool while rollback completes (will reduce their queueing).
- Apply temporary routing policy to shift new requests to the unaffected region subset.

Mid-term (1–6h):
- Full rollback and validation, then controlled re-deploy with canary + stricter health-check gating (we'll add a sequence-length-weighted probe).
- Postmortem to include revert gating and a cost/latency regression dashboard for customer-facing models.

I attached a utilization snapshot (pool-utilization-snapshot-20260818.png) and the incident runbook link for the bridge. If we authorize emergency capacity for Monetary.ai we'll need exec sign-off on the temporary commit changes (billing/credit implications below).

Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Success — Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pool-utilization-snapshot-20260818.png, incident_runbook_link.txt
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Monetary.ai reserved capacity regression - exec decision required

Looping in execs and finance as discussed. Forwarding the thread with the current remediation/mitigation plan. Action items for leadership:
1) Approve a 24-hour emergency reserved capacity bump (add two nodes) for Monetary.ai to restore their throughput immediately. Estimated incremental cost to Redwood: ~$9,600 for 24 hours.
2) Approve customer-facing remediation credit up to $12k if SLA thresholds are missed for their billed period (to be reconciled after postmortem).
3) Decision on priority engineering allocation: continue with the hotfix rollback or halt and run a deeper canary (Marissa recommends rollback + canary).

If leadership approves, we will: (a) provision capacity now, (b) enact rollback on affected fleet, (c) schedule a 1PM PT readout for Monetary.ai with a timeline and compensation summary.

Please reply with APPROVE or DENY and any changes to the amounts above.

— Rishi
VP, Sales Operations (acting on escalation)
Redwood Inference
